hints: Focus on what must be present for a liquid or solution to conduct electricity, mobile charged particles.
Y conducts well both as a pure liquid and in water, so think which type of lattice gives mobile ions in both cases.
Z is non-conducting as a pure liquid but gives a conducting mixture with water, so look for a covalent chloride that reacts with water to release ions.
walkthrough:
**Understand what conductivity tells us**

Think side by side with me. Conduction needs mobile ions or electrons.

In a molten ionic compound, ions are free to move, so it conducts well. In a pure covalent molecular liquid, there are no ions, so it does not conduct.

**Identify Y**

Y is good in the liquid state and good in water.

That is classic ionic behaviour. Molten ions move and conduct:
$$\text{NaCl(l)} \rightarrow \text{Na}^{+}(\text{mobile}) + \text{Cl}^{-}(\text{mobile})$$
And in water it dissolves to give mobile hydrated ions, so it conducts again. $\text{NaCl}$ fits perfectly.

**Identify Z**

Z does not conduct as a liquid, but conducts after adding to water.

That means Z itself is molecular covalent with no ions. $\text{SiCl}_{4}$ is a simple covalent liquid, so no conduction.

With water it hydrolyses to give ions:
$$\text{SiCl}_{4} + 4\text{H}_{2}\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Si(OH)}_{4} + 4\text{H}^{+} + 4\text{Cl}^{-}$$
Those $\text{H}^{+}$ and $\text{Cl}^{-}$ ions make the mixture conduct well. So Y is $\text{NaCl}$ and Z is $\text{SiCl}_{4}$.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{Al}_{2}\text{O}_{3}$ is ionic and would conduct when molten, but it is insoluble in water and does not give a conducting solution, so it cannot be Y. $\text{SiCl}_{4}$ is correct for Z, but Y is wrong.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{NaCl}$ is correct for Y, but $\text{Al}_{2}\text{O}_{3}$ cannot be Z. Molten $\text{Al}_{2}\text{O}_{3}$ conducts, whereas Z does not conduct in the liquid state. Also $\text{Al}_{2}\text{O}_{3}$ is insoluble and gives no ions in water.
options.C: Correct. Y is $\text{NaCl}$, a giant ionic lattice that gives mobile ions both when molten and when dissolved in water, so good conduction in both. Z is $\text{SiCl}_{4}$, a covalent molecular liquid with no ions so non-conducting, but it hydrolyses in water to form $\text{H}^{+}$ and $\text{Cl}^{-}$ ions which conduct well.
options.D: Incorrect. This reverses the logic. $\text{SiCl}_{4}$ as a pure covalent liquid does not conduct, so it cannot be Y. $\text{Al}_{2}\text{O}_{3}$ conducts when molten and does not dissolve to give ions, so it cannot be Z.
